links.outcome: Readability of AI-generated spinal surgery patient education materials (FKRE, FKGL, SMOG)
links.effect: Average FKRE 43.02 to 57.16, FKGL 9.12 to 13.34, SMOG 8.90 to 11.84; advanced junior high to early university level, above recommended health-literacy levels.
links.quote: The average FKRE ranged from 43.02 to 57.16 ("difficult" to "standard English"), FKGL from 9.12 to 13.34, and SMOG from 8.90 to 11.84, corresponding to reading levels from advanced junior high to early university.

links.outcome: Plain-language comprehensibility of AI-generated patient education materials
links.effect: Readability remained above recommended health-literacy levels (FKGL 9.12 to 13.34); clinician review and plain-language optimization needed before patient use.
links.quote: Readability remains above recommended health- literacy levels, and clinician review and plain-language optimization are required before patient use.

links.outcome: Presence of verifiable references in AI-generated patient education content
links.effect: Verifiable references were absent from the generated materials; factual accuracy was not independently verified.
links.quote: Readability remained challenging, and verifiable references were absent.

unlisted_practices: Assessing inter-generation stability of LLM outputs across repeated generations of the same prompt
Rating quality of patient education materials with the DISCERN instrument

screen.reason: The study evaluates the readability, stability, and quality of patient education materials generated by ChatGPT-5.4 for spinal surgery without testing a specific organizational deployment safeguard or practice intervention.
